rawFindings.title: Incorrect res.format behavior when only default is provided
rawFindings.explanation: The line 'var key = req.accepts(keys);' causes a regression by removing the prior condition that handled the case when 'keys.length === 0'. Previously, if there were no keys and only a 'default' property, it correctly set 'key' to false, allowing the 'default' handler to run. The new code sets 'key' to req.accepts([]), which returns null, leading to incorrect behavior and runtime error with only 'default' handler.
rawFindings.suggestion:
Restore the original logic to handle empty keys array as before:
  var key = keys.length > 0
    ? req.accepts(keys)

rawFindings.title: Incorrect handling of .format() when only default handler provided
rawFindings.explanation: The original code checked if keys.length > 0 before calling req.accepts(keys). This was necessary because when only a 'default' handler is provided in res.format, keys would be an empty array, req.accepts([]) would return false, causing res.format to incorrectly emit a 406 error instead of invoking the default handler. The change removes this check and always calls req.accepts(keys), resulting in key being false when keys is empty. However, this causes the flow to skip the invocation of the 'def
rawFindings.suggestion:
Restore the check for keys.length > 0 before calling req.accepts(keys). Change line 609 back to:

  var key = keys.length > 0 ? req.accepts(keys) : false;
